Deadly airstrike hits Sudan-Egypt border gold mine, killing at least 13 miners
An airstrike killed at least 13 artisanal miners in a border area between Sudan and Egypt where artisanal and small-scale gold mining is widespread, a medical group said Sunday.
The strike Saturday in the Border Triangle Area between Sudan, Egypt and Libya, and also wounded at least 28 others, according to the Sudan Doctors Network, which tracks the conflict in Sudan.
It wasn’t immediately clear who was behind the strike. The network, however, said the miners were repeatedly warned by Egyptian authorities to evacuate the area, which is reportedly part of Egypt.
Gold has played a central part in the war in Sudan, with the insurgent paramilitary Rapid Support Forces smuggling out thousands of tons of gold from the Darfur and Kordofan regions to fund themselves.
Abdel-Aziz Yousef, a survivor, told The Associated Press that an unknown aircraft struck an artisanal gold mine in a mountainous area Saturday morning.
He said that many people were killed or wounded, and others fled the area for fear of further strikes.
The medical group said the death toll is likely to increase given that some of the wounded have suffered from serious injuries and limited access to healthcare facilities.
In June, Egyptian security forces detained hundreds of people, including foreigners, on the border with Sudan, accusing them of illegal gold mining and smuggling.
More than 50% of gold mined in Sudan was smuggled out of the country, according to a U.N. Panel of Experts Report in 2024.

articles.title: Adversaries have given up on military victory, IRGC adviser says
articles.body:
Adversaries have given up on military victory, IRGC adviser says
TEHRAN — Brigadier General Mohammad Reza Naqdi, a senior adviser to the commander-in-chief of Iran’s Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC), said on Sunday that Iran’s adversaries had lost hope of achieving their objectives through military confrontation and were increasingly relying on economic pressure and internal divisions.
Speaking in Birjand, Naqdi argued that the United States had failed to achieve its strategic objectives in previous military interventions, citing Afghanistan and Iraq as examples. Despite enormous financial costs, military occupations and substantial casualties, Washington ultimately withdrew from both countries.
According to Naqdi, those experiences have demonstrated the limits of US military power and reinforced the difficulties Washington would face in attempting a ground invasion of Iran.
The senior IRGC adviser also highlighted the capabilities of Iran’s naval and aerospace forces, saying the country’s missile power had altered the military calculations of its adversaries.
He warned that any renewed US air or missile attack on Iran would be met with a stronger response, arguing that the country’s defensive capabilities had made the potential costs of further military action clear to Washington.
Naqdi further warned that, if attacks were repeated, Iran could target economic and petrochemical facilities as well as strategic infrastructure, including artificial intelligence-related systems in the region.
He also stated that some of the enemy's military bases in the region had been severely damaged in previous attacks.
Naqdi said Iran’s adversaries had increasingly shifted their focus toward economic pressure and efforts to deepen domestic divisions after failing to secure a military victory.
Their objective, he argued, was to weaken national cohesion and create conditions for renewed hostile action.
He called on the public and officials to remain vigilant and preserve national unity, saying a united country would prevent adversaries from exploiting domestic differences.
Naqdi also described the departure of US naval forces from the Persian Gulf as evidence of 'the failure of Washington’s regional military strategy.'

articles.title: Zelenskyy ready for fresh elections in Ukraine if Russia agrees to truce
articles.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, following critical comments from US President Donald Trump that he will organise elections in Ukraine if Russian President Vladimir Putin agrees to a 60-day ceasefire.
"Please tell Putin, give us two months, 60 days of total ceasefire, 60 days, and we will organise elections," Zelenskyy told ABC.
Trump on Saturday criticised Zelenskyy for attacking Russian oil refineries a day after the US temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian fuel that were designed to deprive Moscow of revenues to fund its war in Ukraine.
"I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president."
Trump had told reporters at the White House.
In response, Zelenskyy said "it's up to Ukrainians" to choose their leader and noted that Putin would also like to change who is leading Ukraine.
He said it is easy for Ukraine to be blamed for higher fuel prices "when everybody in the world understands (that) because of the war in (the) Middle East, the prices are rising."
Earlier on Sunday, Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready to halt attacks on Russian oil refineries if Moscow ceases its own strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

articles.title: Yemeni army bombs Houthi positions amid ongoing military escalation
articles.body:
Mohammed Sameai and Serdar Dincel
11 October 2026•Update: 11 October 2026
The Yemeni army launched airstrikes on Houthi positions in the southwestern province of Taiz amid military escalation across the country.
In a statement, the army’s Taiz Military Axis said airstrikes targeted Houthi positions, gatherings and vehicles at al-Maqrami, al-Jaasha and al-Sallal hills east of Taiz city, as well as Hisn al-Mukhaf and the Bala’an area on the Aqrouz front in the south of the province.
It did not provide any details about possible casualties or damage.
In Sanaa, Yemeni media outlets, including the independent Yemen Future platform, reported separate strikes in the capital but did not identify who carried them out or specify if there were any casualties or damage.
In Saada, the Houthi-run Saba news agency reported six Saudi airstrikes in Majz district and Saada city. Rocket fire was also reported in Sahar district.
Meanwhile, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree vowed that his group would continue attacks on Saudi airports, despite international and UN calls to halt the strikes.
In a post on the US social media company X, Saree warned airlines, aviation personnel and travelers against using Saudi airports and airspace, saying they could be targeted.
The Houthi threat came a day after 12 people were killed and 309 others injured in a Houthi strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday, according to the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation.
The deadly attack came as fighting has escalated in Yemen since July and spilled into neighboring Saudi Arabia.
Yemen has been engulfed in war since the Houthis seized control of Sanaa and several provinces in September 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the Yemeni government.

articles.title: Tehran hosts art exhibition, live painting workshop on True Promise
articles.body:
Tehran hosts art exhibition, live painting workshop on True Promise
TEHRAN- The second edition of the painting exhibition and live art workshop “True Promise in the Mirror of Art” is currently underway at Palestine Square in Tehran, with artists and members of the public taking part in the event.
The program runs daily from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. and will continue until October 16, Mehr reported.
The event is part of the visual arts section of the second international “True Promise in the Mirror of Art” program. It is hosted by the Greater Tehran Basij of Artists, in cooperation with the Basij unit of the National Iranian Oil Products Distribution Company and the artistic affairs department of the Foundation of Martyrs and Veterans Affairs’ cultural and educational deputy, the report added.
During the workshop, visual artists create works alongside members of the public, drawing on themes related to Iran’s “True Promise” operations and their artistic representation.
Other subjects include the leadership, lifestyle, governing approach and the martyrdom of the late Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, as well as what the organizers describe as Iran’s strength, courage and strategic capabilities during the 12-day conflict and the Ramadan War.
The program also addresses themes of sacrifice and martyrdom through visual art.
The second international “True Promise in the Mirror of Art” event is organized by the Basij Organization of Artists, with Mohammad Najjari serving as its secretary.
The “True Promise” operations are a series of Iranian military actions launched in response to Israeli attacks. The first operation, in April 2024, involved missile and drone strikes against Israel following an Israeli attack on Iran’s diplomatic compound in Damascus on April 1. A second operation took place in October 2024, after the killing of senior figures in Iran and allied groups. In June 2025, Iran launched Operation True Promise III in retaliation for Israeli strikes on Iranian territory, during the 12-day conflict. The operations have become a prominent theme in Iran’s official discourse on national defense and are also reflected in cultural and artistic events.
SAB/

articles.title: How extreme boredom can push people toward aggressive behavior
articles.body:
Boredom might be more than just a fleeting annoyance; it could actually drive people toward aggressive behavior. A new paper suggests that experiencing intense boredom increases the desire for sensation and stimulation, which in turn can lead to both physical aggression and support for military conflict. These findings were published in Personality and Individual Differences.
Psychologists usually define aggression as any behavior explicitly aimed at harming or injuring another living being. Over the decades, researchers have identified biological factors like hormone levels and environmental factors like social rejection that contribute to hostile tendencies.
Recently, some psychologists have begun to explore the role of boredom in aggressive acts. Previous research has linked boredom to everyday sadism, which is the derivation of pleasure from inflicting suffering on others.
It remained unknown whether boredom also drives non-sadistic aggression, which does not require the aggressor to feel pleasure from someone else’s pain. People often experience boredom as an unpleasant emotional state defined by a lack of meaning and an inability to engage with their current environment.
Heng Li, a researcher at Sichuan International Studies University in China, designed a series of studies to test the boundaries of boredom and aggression. Li proposed that boredom acts as a psychological signal prompting people to seek out highly arousing experiences to restore a sense of meaning.
This pursuit of high-arousal experiences is known in psychology as sensation seeking. Because sensation seeking can reduce a person’s inhibitions and narrow their focus to immediate thrills, Li suspected it might push bored individuals toward aggressive actions.
To establish a baseline connection, Li first surveyed 180 Chinese university students and 190 Vietnamese university students. The participants completed standardized questionnaires measuring their general tendency to experience boredom in daily life, as well as their hostile tendencies.
The survey assessed physical aggression, verbal aggression, anger, and hostility. By studying both Chinese and Vietnamese populations, the research expanded beyond the Western, industrialized nations that typically dominate psychology samples.
Li found a positive association between the propensity to experience boredom and aggressive traits. In both groups of university students, those who reported feeling bored more often also reported higher levels of trait aggression. The relationship held true across all four subcomponents of hostile behavior.
Because surveys only measure self-reported tendencies, Li conducted a second study to test physical behavior. This experiment involved 124 non-student adults in China.
Participants were randomly assigned to one of two video-watching conditions. In the boredom group, people watched a monotonous 25-minute video of a man repeatedly folding laundry. In the control group, participants watched an engaging 25-minute documentary about a local park.
After watching the videos, participants filled out a questionnaire designed to measure their current desire for sensation seeking. A researcher then escorted them to a separate room with a punching bag and provided boxing gloves.
The researcher told the participants to punch the bag for as long as they wanted, explaining that they would evaluate the punching experience afterward. A concealed camera recorded the activity, and independent raters later evaluated the force and comfort level of the punches.
The results showed that participants in the boredom condition delivered more punches than those in the control group. The bored participants also punched the bag harder, appeared more comfortable doing so, and reported enjoying the activity more.
Statistical analyses revealed that sensation seeking mediated this effect. The tedious laundry video increased participants’ desire for stimulation, which directly predicted their increased physical aggression toward the punching bag.
A final experiment tested whether this mechanism applies to real-world political aggression. Li recruited 277 American adults through an online platform, ensuring a mix of liberal and conservative voters.
As in the previous experiment, participants were randomly assigned to watch either a boring video of a water wall or a more engaging documentary. They then answered questions about their current sensation-seeking desires.
Following the video and sensation-seeking survey, the participants read hypothetical scenarios involving international conflicts. They were asked to imagine themselves as the commander-in-chief and rate their level of support for aggressive military action against Iran.
The scenarios included situations where foreign military entities trained insurgents or blatantly disregarded the international community. Higher agreement on the survey indicated a stronger endorsement of violent military solutions.
Li found that conservatives generally exhibited more support for military strikes than liberals. However, the boredom manipulation increased support for war across the entire political spectrum.
Both liberal and conservative participants who watched the boring water wall video reported higher sensation-seeking scores and greater support for military aggression than those who watched the documentary. Once again, sensation seeking served as the bridge linking the tedious experience to the hostile response.
While the experiments demonstrate that boredom can cause aggressive behavior in laboratory and hypothetical settings, human decision-making relies on many other variables. A person’s baseline level of self-control may alter how they respond to a lack of stimulation.
People with high self-control might resist aggressive impulses even when they feel intensely under-stimulated. Future studies could test whether diminished self-control worsens the aggressive responses seen in bored individuals.
It is also easy to misinterpret these results as proof that boredom inevitably leads to violence. Aggression is just one possible pathway people use to escape an existential void.
Other research shows that people often cope with boredom through positive or neutral behaviors, such as engaging in creative hobbies, physical exercise, or nostalgic daydreaming. Providing people with constructive, high-arousal activities can help channel sensation-seeking urges away from hostility during times of extreme monotony.
The study, “Bored to battle: The relationship between boredom and aggression,” was authored by Heng Li.

articles.title: Mystery object enters Israel from Lebanon, vanishes as IDF searches for answers | Watch
articles.body:
More than 12 hours after a suspected drone infiltration triggered an alert in the Western Galilee on Saturday evening, the IDF still does not know what the unidentified aerial object was that crossed from Lebanon into Israel and disappeared. Among the possibilities being investigated is that it was a drone model unfamiliar to Israel's defense establishment.
Security camera footage from the area, published by ynet for the first time, shows the unidentified object that triggered the alert.
Moshe Davidovich, head of the Mateh Asher Regional Council and chairman of the Confrontation Line Forum, told residents Sunday morning that after the suspicious object was spotted, security forces raised their alert level and conducted searches throughout the night.
"Emergency teams and local security coordinators were updated and operated throughout the night," Davidovich said. "Following a situation assessment, it was decided to return to routine, alongside continued security operations and the presence of checkpoints."
He added: "We are aware of the questions raised by the incident, and because of the lack of clarity, I urgently contacted the Northern Command commander this morning to demand an immediate meeting with me and all the heads of the frontline local authorities, to receive a full, clear and unequivocal investigation into the incident."
The IDF issued its first official statement only about four hours after the object crossed the border.
"Following the alert activated at 7:57 p.m. in Arab al-Aramshe, IDF observation posts identified an unidentified aerial object near the border with Lebanon," the military said. "IDF forces are continuing searches in the area. So far, no unusual findings have been discovered. There are no special instructions for civilians."
Following the alert, the IDF deployed large numbers of troops to communities across the Western Galilee to rule out the possibility of an infiltration.
Forces were dispatched to Adamit, Arab al-Aramshe, Ya'ara, Goren, Hanita, Shlomi, Gesher Haziv, Sa'ar, Kabri, Avdon, Betzet, Liman, Nahariya, Evron, Ben Ami, Matzuba and Rosh Hanikra.
Helicopters were also scrambled to assist with aerial searches, and the sound of their engines was clearly heard throughout the area.
Searches continued Sunday morning, both on the ground and from the air, as security forces attempted to determine what had happened and identify the object.
The IDF said residents could maintain their normal routines and that no special Home Front Command instructions had been issued. Nevertheless, many members of the local rapid-response teams activated Saturday evening in communities near the Lebanese border remained on duty as the searches continued.
During the night, security forces also investigated additional suspicions, including a possible infiltration from the sea near Nahariya. Those concerns were subsequently ruled out.
First published: 08:49, 10.11.26

articles.title: Tehran showcases urban market management, food security expertise to foreign delegations
articles.body:
Tehran showcases urban market management, food security expertise to foreign delegations
TEHRAN- Tehran Municipality’s first program in the series of specialized visits “Introducing Tehran’s Urban Management Capabilities,” focusing on urban markets, logistics, and food security, was held on Saturday, October 10, in cooperation with the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) and the Asian Mayors Forum (AMF).
In this program, representatives of foreign countries and international organizations visited the Jalal Al-e Ahmad Fruit and Vegetable Market and the Beihaghi Shahrvand Store and became acquainted with Tehran’s urban management capacities in supplying and distributing essential goods. After these visits, a specialized meeting was held aimed at examining areas for joint cooperation.
This program, held under the title “Specialized Visit to Tehran’s Urban Markets, Logistics and Food Security” by the International Deputy of the Communication Center of Tehran Municipality, was welcomed by those present.
The purpose of this measure was also to develop urban diplomacy and introduce Tehran’s management capacities to representatives of international organizations.
During the visit to the Shahrvand Store, a press conference was held in the administrative section of the store. Davood Qorbanian, CEO of Shahrvand Store; Mehdi Bakhtiari-Zadeh, CEO of the Organization of Markets; Hamid Reza Gholamzadeh, Head of the Communication and International Affairs Center of Tehran Municipality, as well as the Secretary-General of the Asian Mayors Forum; and Mohammad Ali Shafiei, International Deputy of the Communication and International Affairs Center of Tehran Municipality, were present, and specialized topics concerning urban market management, supply of goods, and food security were discussed.
Fruit and vegetable markets ready to transfer experience and develop export of Iranian products
The CEO of the Organization for Management of Fruit and Vegetable Markets of Tehran Municipality, referring to the capacity of the capital’s market network, announced the organization’s readiness to develop international cooperation in the fields of transferring technical knowledge, supplying and distributing food products, and expanding exports of Iranian products.
Emphasizing the municipality’s responsibility to ensure citizens’ food security, he said: Access to high-quality, healthy, and reasonably priced food products is one of the main axes of the municipality’s activity. In this regard, an extensive network of fruit and vegetable markets and Shahrvand stores has been formed across the city.
Bakhtiari-Zadeh added: Currently, about 320 fruit and vegetable markets are active in Tehran, and citizens can, on average, access one of the municipality’s food product distribution centers by traveling less than 900 meters.
Referring to quality control mechanisms, he said: To ensure the health of products, a direct supply chain and continuous testing are on the agenda, and goods that do not meet the required quality and health standards will not be allowed to enter the markets covered by the organization.
The CEO of the Organization for Management of Fruit and Vegetable Markets of Tehran Municipality, referring to the capacity for cooperation with the countries present at the meeting, stated: This complex can cooperate in transferring technical knowledge, exchanging experience, and presenting models of management and distribution of food products.
Referring to Iran’s agricultural capacity and the production of diverse products in different seasons of the year, he added: Cooperation with traders and economic actors can provide the basis for developing the export of fruit and vegetable products and protein products.
Bakhtiari-Zadeh noted: Currently, trade in agricultural products between Iran and some of the countries present at this meeting exists, and cooperation with Tehran Municipality’s extensive network can help strengthen these relations and develop export routes.
In the end, he expressed hope that this visit would pave the way for expanding commercial and technical cooperation with friendly countries and forming more sustainable relations in the field of supply, distribution, and export of food products.
Shahrvand ready to develop commercial cooperation and exchange experience with foreign companies
Davood Qorbanian, CEO of Shahrvand Company, also emphasizing the necessity of expanding international cooperation, said: Familiarizing representatives of countries and embassies with Tehran Municipality’s services can pave the way for strengthening relations among countries and developing commercial and trade communications.
Referring to the company’s capacities for cooperation with trade and retail actors in various countries, he stated: Shahrvand is ready to provide the ground for the exchange of knowledge, experience, and technology and the development of commercial exchanges. In this regard, we invite the representatives of the countries present to introduce capable companies from their countries to begin joint cooperation.
Qorbanian, who is also the vice chairman of the country’s Chain Stores Union, added: The possibility of developing communications and exchanging experience exists not only for Shahrvand Company but also for other chain stores in Iran.
Stating that Iran enjoys significant capacities in the production of agricultural products and foodstuffs, as well as a broad consumer market, he said: Foreign companies can identify new opportunities for developing their commercial activities by understanding the needs of the Iranian market.
The CEO of Shahrvand Company continued: The areas of cooperation are not limited only to the supply of food, agricultural products, and meat; they also include the field of retail technologies, including enterprise resource planning (ERP) software, store management, and marketing systems. Shahrvand Company is ready to benefit from the specialized knowledge and experience of foreign companies in these areas.
Qorbanian at this meeting, referring to the role of Shahrvand stores and fruit markets, added: Iranian producers and industries can use the capacity of Shahrvand stores to offer products, introduce brands, and access the consumer market. In return, this company can be a platform for introducing and offering products of various countries in the Iranian market; a cooperation that includes areas such as raw materials, agricultural and food products, packaged goods, and retail-related technologies.
He asked the representatives of the countries present to provide the ground for communication with capable companies and economic actors through their commercial counselors and the economic sections of their embassies.
In the end, Qorbanian expressed hope that these visits would lead to practical and sustainable cooperation among Shahrvand Company, Iranian traders, and foreign companies and provide the ground for market development, exchange of knowledge and technology, and mutual supply of the parties’ commercial needs.
Tehran municipality seeks to turn sister-city relations into practical economic cooperation
The Secretary-General of the Asian Mayors Forum at this meeting emphasized using the capacity of relations among cities to develop commercial cooperation, transfer experiences, and engage economic companies.
Referring to Tehran’s experience in large-scale distribution of goods and maintaining citizens’ access to essential products, he spoke of the capacity for cooperation with regional cities in the fields of export and import of products, transfer of technical knowledge, and provision of urban services.
Gholamzadeh also introduced the “Zero Inflation” initiative, aimed at stabilizing the prices of 12 essential goods for six months, as one of Tehran Municipality’s measures to support citizens.
Foreign diplomats emphasize Tehran’s capacity in supplying and distributing essential goods
At the end of the program, representatives of foreign countries and the Deputy Secretary-General of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO), in conversations with reporters, considered Tehran’s capacities in supplying and distributing food to be significant.
ECO emphasizes Tehran urban management’s role in strengthening regional food security
The Deputy Secretary-General of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) also considered the city’s experience in supplying and distributing food valuable and emphasized the role of municipalities in strengthening food security and citizens’ affordable access to essential goods even in crisis conditions.
Emre Hengut also called for the continuation of specialized visits and the exchange of experiences to develop cooperation among cities and regional institutions.
The list of guests present in the half-day tour organized by Tehran Municipality, included Kim Junpyo, Ambassador of South Korea, and his wife; Ahmad Soueidan, Ambassador of Lebanon; Khalid Ibrahim Elsheikh, Deputy Head of Mission in the Sudanese Embassy; Bahador Nazir, Counsellor of the Tajik Embassy; Mostafa Diabate, Counselor of the Burkina Faso Embassy; Vladislav Perpelkin, Counselor of the Russian Embassy; Hubert Przybyszewski, First Secretary of the Polish Embassy; Deputy Ambassador of Oman; Faizan Taimoor Saqib, Third Secretary in Embassy of Pakistan, Counselor of the Pakistani Embassy; Jadidzadeh, Economic Officer of the United Nations Coordinator’s Office; Chentaei Emre Angut, Deputy Secretary-General of ECO; and Lola Gheybollahzadeh, Head of ECO Coordination and Follow-up Department.
Overall, the specialized visit served as a practical step in strengthening Tehran’s urban diplomacy and presenting its integrated network of fruit and vegetable markets and Shahrvand stores as a working model for food supply, price regulation, and access to essential goods.
By bringing together foreign ambassadors, international organizations such as ECO and the Asian Mayors Forum, and Tehran Municipality officials, the program created a platform for exchanging technical knowledge, expanding trade in agricultural and food products, and encouraging joint investment and retail cooperation.
If followed by concrete agreements and sustained follow-up, such initiatives could help transform sister-city and international relations into tangible economic partnerships, enhance regional food security, and open new export and knowledge-exchange opportunities for both Iran and participating countries.

articles.title: IDF advances Yellow Line deeper into Gaza, Palestinian reports say
articles.body:
According to reports from Gaza, IDF forces operating in the Gaza Strip have pushed the Yellow Line forward by dozens of meters. Three years after the October 7 massacre, the IDF controls approximately 64% of the Gaza Strip, with two divisions deployed across a broad area and about 30 military outposts.
Israeli defense officials say the military's defensive lines have been completely overhauled since the massacre and the failures that preceded it. Pushing the Yellow Line forward serves several operational purposes. It allows the IDF to improve its operational control in areas where it detects significant Hamas efforts to regroup or indications that terrorists intend to carry out attacks or launch terrorist operations from those locations.
"Even if Hamas tries to do something, it will encounter IDF forces positioned on the front line. Our defense does not begin at the border fence but deeper inside the territory," a senior defense official told ynet and Yedioth Ahronoth.
Since October 7, holding territory has become a cornerstone of the IDF's offensive defense strategy across most fronts, particularly in Gaza, Syria and Lebanon. The idea is not to wait for the enemy to reach Israeli communities but to establish a buffer zone where threats can be identified, intercepted and confronted before they reach populated areas.
The IDF did not always embrace this approach. For years leading up to October 7, 2023, Israel's defense doctrine was built around intelligence and technological superiority. Oct. 7 exposed the limitations of a doctrine focused primarily on preventing surprise attacks. The failure went deeper than the lack of an intelligence warning and the inability to prevent the surprise assault: The IDF was not prepared to fight such an attack once it was underway. That lesson is now being applied in different ways across all fronts.
In Gaza, the IDF has shifted from a defense strategy centered on defending the border to one focused on shaping the territory beyond it. The military controls key routes, operates outposts and forward positions and continues efforts to locate and dismantle underground infrastructure in areas under its control.
This marks a dramatic departure from the defense doctrine that prevailed before the massacre, when the military's instructions were to defend the border and enter Gaza when necessary. The question today is not simply how much territory the IDF holds, but how long it can maintain control, at what cost and with how many troops.
The military is pursuing a similar approach on other fronts, including Lebanon and Syria. The lesson drawn from the failures of three years ago is the need to establish defensive depth and maintain a presence on the ground, creating a security buffer of roughly 10 kilometers (6 miles), while conducting operations aimed at pushing threats farther away and preventing hostile forces from reestablishing themselves.
This new defense strategy also requires a larger deployment of forces. Some 40,000 reservists have been added to the military's personnel roster since the start of the war, tens of thousands of reservists have been reassigned, approximately 30 battalions have been added to the military's operational force structure and mandatory military service has been extended to 32 months.
New formations have been established, additional battalions and rapid-response units have been created and drone and remotely piloted aircraft capabilities have been expanded. Intelligence-gathering and firepower capabilities have also been strengthened, while new formations have been established to provide greater military strength within each operational sector.
Beyond the operational costs, holding territory also carries a price on the international stage. Israel is already facing U.S. pressure to withdraw from areas it captured in southern Lebanon. The IDF's new strategy is also hampering normalization with Arab countries, which are increasingly alarmed by what they perceive as a "plot to expand Israeli territory at their expense."

articles.title: Netanyahu demands probe into sources of award-winning Gaza film
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Netanyahu demands probe into Israeli whistleblowers cited in award-winning Gaza film
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called on Sunday for an investigation into the anonymous sources featured in the award-winning Gaza war documentary "NAZA".
The film is based on testimony from 24 unnamed Israeli military whistleblowers who accuse the army of killing scores of civilians in Gaza with the use of AI-powered targeting systems.
"Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu this evening asked the chief of staff of the Israeli army, the head of the Shin Bet (domestic intelligence), and the state attorney to open a thorough investigation targeting the participants in the film 'NAZA' and to prosecute them," Netanyahu's office said in a statement.
"NAZA" takes its name from the Israeli military term for civilian casualties expected in airstrikes, an abbreviated form of the Hebrew phrase for "collateral damage".
Awarded a special jury prize at the Venice Film Festival, the film received a historic 25-minute standing ovation. The film has received praise around the world for revealing the extent of Israel's atrocities in Gaza, but has triggered a political storm in Israel.
"This film tells a false, misleading and biased story that defames the State of Israel and the army around the world," Netanyahu said, according to the statement.
He has previously declared his intention to back legislation to strip citizenship from people who "defame" soldiers.
Israel's military campaign in Gaza, determined to be a genocide by scholars and rights groups, has killed more than 74,000 people, according to the territory's health ministry.
The war on Gaza has also devastated the enclave's healthcare system, displaced the majority of the population and levelled entire neighbourhoods.

articles.title: At least 139 migrants dead after boat to Yemen capsizes
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
At least 139 migrants dead, including some children, after boat from Djibouti to Yemen capsizes
At least 139 migrants, including at least 15 children, have died and around 84 are missing after a boat carrying more than 300 people capsized while sailing from Djibouti to Yemen, the United Nations International Organisation for Migration said on Sunday.
The boat, carrying 305 people, capsized near Guhere, north of Obock, a port town in Djibouti, during the night of 8-9 October, the IOM said, citing survivor accounts.
Around 82 people survived the shipwreck, the statement said. An Ethiopian government spokesperson did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Photographs shared by the UN agency showed worn-out sandals and sneakers washed up on the shore.
"Our teams are on the ground alongside local authorities to provide emergency assistance," said Alexandre Coissac, IOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti.
"This tragedy is a stark reminder of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek economic opportunities," Coissac said.
Djiboutian authorities are continuing search and rescue operations, the IOM statement said, adding that local authorities are also providing medical care to survivors and arranging burials for the deceased.
The Djibouti government could not be immediately reached for comment.
The migrants were heading to Yemen, with the hope of eventually making it to wealthier Gulf nations, even as Yemeni nationals themselves flee their country, which is experiencing the most serious escalation in fighting between Saudi Arabia-backed government forces and the Iran-backed Houthis since a UN-brokered truce in 2022. 
"Despite the violence in Yemen, migrants are still making the perilous journeys hoping to make it to the Gulf countries," the IOM statement said.
Fighting in Ethiopia
Fighting has also broken out in Ethiopia since last month in the biggest escalation of violence since the 2020-2022 Tigray war.
An IOM official told Reuters that the UN agency had documented heavy migrant traffic along the so-called Eastern Route through Djibouti for several years.
"People continue to use the route amid changing conditions in Ethiopia and Yemen, although the volume and direction of movement can shift over time," the official said.
Ethiopian migrants interviewed for the agency's most recent situation report on Djibouti from 20 September to 30 September said they left their country because of difficult living conditions, including the impact of drought.
"Some migrants also reported that they were fleeing conflict and forced recruitment by armed forces," the report said.
Multiple residents of Tigray, where fighting erupted on 23 September, have told Reuters that they had seen Tigrayan rebels forcibly recruit young men into the defence forces. The rebels have denied conducting forced recruitment.
The conflict has sparked fears of a return to all-out war, with Ethiopia and Eritrea severing relations over alleged Eritrean support for the rebel alliance seeking to overthrow Ethiopia's government. Eritrea has denied backing the alliance.
Severe risks
The so-called Eastern Route presents many dangers, including accidents at sea, trafficking and arbitrary arrests once on land. In 2025, more than 900 migrants died or went missing along the route, according to IOM's Missing Migrants Project, as the number of people undertaking the journey increased by 18 percent.
IOM has described the crisis sparked by the fighting in Yemen as alarming, with displacement figures surging to 200,000 from 76,000 in mid-September, according to data released by the agency last week.
More than 3,700 people have fled Yemen by sea to Djibouti as of last week, it said.

articles.title: Ethiopian official promises change in Tigray
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Ethiopian official promises change in Tigray after troops retake regional capital
A former Tigray leader, now advising Ethiopia's prime minister, promised a "visible change" in the region on Sunday after government-allied units retook Mekelle city following renewed fighting with opposition forces.
Ethiopian Airlines resumed flights to the city of Mekelle on Sunday for the first time since rebels led by the Tigray People's Liberation Front seized the airport on 23 September. They withdrew on 3 October, when government-allied fighters entered the city.
Renewed fighting in Tigray has undermined the 2022 peace agreement that ended a two-year war, as mounting tensions between Ethiopia and neighbouring Eritrea have raised fears of a wider conflict.
"I would like to assure you on this occasion that we will bring visible change, a change beyond mere hope," Getachew Reda, an adviser to Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, told supporters who greeted him and intelligence chief Redwan Hussein at Mekelle airport. He did not elaborate.
The 2020-2022 war in Tigray caused about 500,000 civilian deaths from violence, famine and the collapse of health services, according to researchers at Ghent University in Belgium.
The Tigray People's Liberation Front joined six other opposition groups last month in an alliance seeking to oust Abiy.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres urged all parties on Friday to cease hostilities and resume dialogue. He warned that fighting risked further destabilising the wider region.
Ethiopia told the UN Security Council on Friday that it was taking self-defence measures, accusing Eritrea of sending troops across the border and occupying parts of northern Ethiopia.
Ethiopian authorities previously have accused Eritrea of supporting the TPLF, an allegation Eritrea has denied.
Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos did not specify the measures being taken. His letter to the council did not identify the occupied areas or provide evidence supporting the allegations. The Associated Press could not independently verify the claims.
Eritrean Foreign Minister Osman Saleh urged the council to condemn what he called Ethiopia's "unprovoked declaration of war". His response did not confirm or deny the alleged troop crossings.
The dispute deepens a rift between the two countries whose armies fought together against the TPLF during the 2020-2022 war.

articles.title: Israeli army renews airstrikes, artillery shelling in southern Lebanon despite US deal
articles.body:
The Israeli army launched renewed airstrikes and artillery shelling in several towns in southern Lebanon on Sunday, in the latest violations of a US-sponsored framework deal signed in June.
Israeli warplanes bombed the town of Kfar Tebnit in the Nabatieh district, Lebanon’s National News Agency (NNA) reported.
In the Tyre district, Israeli warplanes struck the town of Mansouri, while artillery shelling hit Majdal Zoun, the agency said.
Overnight, the area between the towns of Mayfadoun and Zawtar al-Sharqiyah was subjected to heavy and concentrated Israeli artillery shelling.
READ: Lebanon looks to EU support for state control of weapons, end to Israeli occupation
The attacks came amid Israel’s ongoing offensive against Lebanon, which began on March 2 and has killed 4,386 people and wounded 12,413 others, according to the latest figures released by Lebanon’s Health Ministry.
On June 26, Beirut and Tel Aviv signed the US-brokered framework arrangement in Washington that provides for a gradual Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory and the deployment of the Lebanese army in areas vacated by Israeli forces.
The Israeli army continues its attacks despite the deal and maintains its occupation of parts of Lebanon, including areas held for decades and others seized during recent wars and military operations.
READ: EU to launch training and support mission for Lebanese army: foreign policy chief

articles.title: US forces strike cargo ship attempting to breach Iran blockade in Gulf of Oman
articles.body:
Ahmet Salih Alacaci
11 October 2026•Update: 11 October 2026
US forces struck and disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman on Saturday after its crew allegedly ignored repeated warnings and attempted to breach Washington's naval blockade against Iran, the US military said.
US Central Command (CENTCOM) said a fighter jet struck the stern of the Panama-flagged M/V Ocean Molica, also known as the Arika Sun, disabling its propulsion system.
The military said no crew members were harmed in the strike. The vessel had previously departed an Iranian port and was attempting to transit regional waters when it was intercepted, according to CENTCOM.
The incident came amid the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, which Washington resumed on July 14, two days after Iran said it had again closed the waterway following the resumption of US attacks on July 8.
CENTCOM said four commercial vessels have been disabled and 135 ships turned away during three months of enforcement.
US forces have also destroyed 10 tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' (IRGC) oil transportation network over the same period, the command said.
Separately, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said Sunday that a tanker caught fire after being struck on its port side by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz. The crew was reported safe.
The IRGC said late Saturday that an oil supertanker had struck a naval mine and exploded while attempting to leave the strait through an unauthorized route.
It was not immediately clear whether the UKMTO and IRGC reports concerned the same vessel or whether either incident was connected to the US strike on the Ocean Molica.
CENTCOM warned commercial vessels to comply with blockade instructions and urged crews operating in the Gulf of Oman and near the Strait of Hormuz to monitor maritime notices and maintain communication with US naval forces.
Tehran has also warned that it could target vessels that use routes other than those designated by Iranian authorities or try to transit the strait without permission.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on Feb. 28 that has killed more than 3,000 people, according to Tehran. Iran retaliated with attacks that killed Americans and Israelis before a ceasefire was reached in April.
The US subsequently carried out additional strikes on Iranian sites amid stalled negotiations between Washington and Tehran, despite the signing of a framework agreement in June.
Talks have remained deadlocked due to disagreements concerning navigation through the strategic waterway.

articles.title: Greater power than US previously failed in battle with Iran
articles.body:
During an interview with Press TV on Saturday, Rezaei said the “US suffered repeated defeats in its confrontation with Iran and has consequently turned to economic warfare out of desperation.”
Iran, rather than the US, would determine when the confrontation ends, he said, stressing that Tehran would continue its resistance until its rightful demands are met.
Addressing the presence of US forces in the region, Rezaei told Press TV that the withdrawal of US forces from Iraq reflected Washington’s failure to impose its military agenda on the region, describing it as a vindication of Iran’s resistance to American military presence in West Asia.
Rezaei further said that more than “30 million Iranians have registered in ‘Janfada’ (Sacrifice for Iran) Campaign to take up arms in the event of US aggression.”
On diplomacy, the official said “Tehran would not return to its previous diplomatic norms,” while stressing that “Iran would never abandon diplomacy altogether.”
The senior official warned that, if Washington launched another act of aggression against Iran, American assets could be targeted, including key data systems and artificial intelligence sensors.
Rezaei also identified Washington and its regional allies as the root of the problem surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz in response to the latest round of US-Israeli aggression, preventing US and allied ships from navigating the strategic waterway.
The move resulted in a significant increase in oil and energy prices across the globe, especially in the US, forcing Washington and the International Energy Agency (IEA) to release their strategic resources several times.
Following the signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Iran and the US in June, Tehran opened the Strait of Hormuz, but after the US violated the MoU by blockading Iranian ports, Iran’s Armed Forces closed the maritime corridor once again.

articles.title: IAI to unveil new tactical radar that seeks out low-flying drones at US's AUSA military expo
articles.body:
Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI) announced on Sunday that it will unveil a new radar solution that can detect low-flying drones from its position suspended high above the ground.
The system, known as POINT@AIR, brings long-range radar detection and persistent surveillance to a compact, highly mobile aerostat platform. The unveiling was made at the Association of the United States Army (AUSA) Annual Meeting & Exposition in Washington, taking place this week.
The radar’s elevated position extends its line of sight beyond terrain and other ground-level obstructions, supporting earlier detection of low-altitude threats, while enabling forces to adapt surveillance coverage as mission requirements evolve.
In that sense, a heavy focus will be on anti-drone defense, an area where Hezbollah exposed IDF weaknesses during the 2026 conflict, leading to significant IDF losses.
The system will not replace MMR radar technology and other radars which are primarily focused on long-range detection, but will supplement them in certain specific areas where the threats, such as drones, are evolving.
Persistent operation, rapid relocation capabilities
Designed for persistent operation and rapid relocation, the system can operate without reliance on permanent infrastructure and can detect and track multiple aerial, maritime, and ground targets.
This is one of the new major issues, given that enemy threats have become more unpredictable regarding where and how they will attack from.
It supports multiple missions simultaneously, prioritizes targets according to operational requirements, and interfaces with command-and-control systems to contribute to an integrated operational picture, signaling the continued move toward greater integration of AI and the full network of sensors.
IAI's CEO Guy Bar Lev: 'Seeing the battlespace is the starting point for every effective defense'
Guy Bar Lev, president and CEO of IAI, said, “Seeing the battlespace is the starting point for every effective defense. The more persistent and comprehensive that view becomes, the better equipped forces are to understand what is unfolding, anticipate threats and act with confidence. IAI is increasingly developing next-generation capabilities that expand the boundaries of situational awareness and provide our customers with greater visibility, flexibility and time to respond.”
Dror Bar, CEO of ELTA Systems and EVP at IAI: “POINT@AIR reflects a fundamental shift in how persistent surveillance can be delivered - bringing sophisticated radar capabilities to an elevated platform that is smaller, more mobile and adaptable to the mission. Our goal was not simply to reduce the size of an existing solution, but to rethink what an aerostat-based radar could achieve. By combining advanced AESA technology, long-range detection and 360-degree coverage in a compact configuration, POINT@AIR gives operators the ability to establish persistent awareness where fixed infrastructure may not be practical.”
Based on the proven ELM-2083 radar family, POINT@AIR incorporates advanced Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) technology, with electronic scanning in both azimuth and elevation combined with mechanical rotation to provide 360-degree coverage.

articles.title: EU chief warns of ‘dangerous escalation’ after Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
articles.body:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Sunday warned that the latest Houthi attack on Riyadh’s airport marked a “dangerous escalation,” describing it as the deadliest such attack on the facility so far, Anadolu reports.
“The deadliest Houthi attack so far on Riyadh’s airport marks a dangerous escalation,” von der Leyen said on US social media company X.
“Our thoughts are with the victims and their families,” she said, expressing solidarity with Saudi Arabia and its people.
Von der Leyen warned that the attacks were contributing to growing instability across the region.
“These attacks by Iran’s proxies are pushing the region into a spiral of violence,” she said.
She also highlighted the broader consequences for international transportation and energy infrastructure.
“They are destabilizing crucial global transport and energy nodes with shockwave sent through the world,” she added.
READ: Saudi Arabia says 3 killed in attacks on Riyadh’s King Khalid airport
Calling for an immediate end to violence targeting civilians, von der Leyen said: “These murderous attacks at civilians must stop at once.”
In the airport attack, four Saudis, two Bangladeshi nationals, and one each from the US, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine, and Sudan were killed, according to the Saudi civil aviation authority.
The injured are being treated at hospitals, with some in critical condition.
The aviation authority said earlier that airport operations were temporarily suspended after the attack, while officials assessed the damage and verified the safety of the airport facilities.
The suspension has disrupted flights, with passengers advised to check with airlines before heading to the airport. Kuwait Airways also canceled Saturday service to Riyadh and return flights, citing the airport’s closure.
The attack comes amid heightened tensions following Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports and facilities in recent days.

articles.title: Araghchi calls for international accountability for environmental destruction in wars
articles.body:
Araghchi calls for international accountability for environmental destruction in wars
TEHRAN — Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has called for stronger international mechanisms to prevent and address environmental destruction during armed conflicts, stressing that the international community must move beyond expressions of concern and ensure effective accountability for those responsible.
Addressing the international conference “Ecocide: The Silent War Crime” in Tehran on Sunday, Araghchi said large-scale environmental destruction during warfare was not merely an ecological concern but an issue directly linked to the right to life, public health, food security, international peace and security, and the rights of future generations.
“Environmental protection must move beyond declarations of commitment and enter the realm of accountability, responsibility and effective international action,” he said, warning that the consequences of environmental damage could persist for years or even decades after hostilities end.
Araghchi emphasized that warfare threatens not only human lives, cities and economic infrastructure but also water resources, soil, air quality, forests, agricultural land, energy infrastructure, natural habitats and biodiversity. The release of hazardous substances, contamination of vital resources and destruction of ecosystems can impose lasting costs on civilian populations long after the fighting has stopped.
Gaza, Lebanon and Iran face lasting environmental damage
Citing Gaza, Lebanon and Iran, Araghchi highlighted the far-reaching environmental consequences of military attacks across the region.
In Gaza, he pointed to the collapse of water and wastewater networks, damage to waste-management systems, contamination of water and soil, coastal pollution, and the accumulation of vast quantities of rubble and potentially hazardous materials.
He noted that the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) has reported unprecedented environmental damage in the Palestinian territory, warning that the destruction of essential infrastructure and contamination of natural resources could affect public health and living conditions for decades.
In Lebanon, Araghchi highlighted damage to forests and agricultural land caused by military attacks and resulting fires. He referred to reports submitted to the United Nations documenting the burning of millions of square meters of land and damage to tens of thousands of olive trees. He also recalled the extensive coastal pollution following attacks on oil-storage facilities, illustrating how damage to industrial infrastructure can generate environmental consequences far beyond the immediate site of an attack.
Turning to Iran, the foreign minister addressed the environmental risks associated with US and Israeli attacks on Iranian oil, refinery and energy facilities in March 2026.
He cited a UNEP assessment from that month concerning attacks on oil facilities in and around urban areas, including Tehran, where fires released hazardous compounds into the environment.
Such pollutants, Araghchi warned, can spread from the atmosphere into soil and water resources and ultimately affect the food chain, creating risks that extend well beyond immediate economic losses.
The consequences are particularly serious for civilians, children and future generations, who may continue to suffer the health and environmental effects of wartime contamination long after the conflict has ended.
International law must ensure accountability
Araghchi stressed that international law must not remain indifferent to environmental destruction and violations of fundamental human rights during armed conflicts.
He called for the effective implementation of international humanitarian law, particularly the principles of distinction and proportionality, alongside a thorough assessment of the direct, indirect and long-term environmental consequences of military operations.
The principle of distinction requires parties to distinguish between military objectives and civilian objects. The principle of proportionality prohibits attacks expected to cause incidental civilian harm excessively in relation to the concrete and direct military advantage anticipated. International humanitarian law also provides specific protection for the natural environment against certain forms of damage during armed conflicts.
Araghchi argued that no state or actor should consider itself above international responsibility. Extensive ecosystem destruction, severe contamination of water and soil, and lasting damage to natural resources must be addressed through effective mechanisms for prevention, independent documentation, damage assessment, compensation and accountability.
He said Iran supports legal and expert discussions aimed at strengthening international environmental protection, including consideration of recognizing ecocide as a distinct international crime.
The concept of ecocide broadly concerns exceptionally severe environmental destruction. Proposals to establish it as a separate international crime have gained attention in international legal discussions, although its precise definition, scope, and legal status remain subjects of debate.
For Iran, Araghchi indicated, strengthening international protection requires moving beyond general declarations and developing practical mechanisms capable of establishing responsibility and addressing the consequences of environmental destruction.
Iran warns against double standards in environmental protection
The foreign minister also warned against double standards and the politicization of environmental issues, insisting that environmental obligations must be applied fairly, transparently and without discrimination.
Environmental protection, he said, must not become a privilege for some countries and an obligation on others.
Araghchi further called for serious examination of the legal, humanitarian and environmental consequences of unilateral coercive measures that restrict countries' access to financing, clean technologies and essential equipment needed to protect the environment, manage ecological emergencies and address climate change.
He argued that environmental justice requires developing countries to have access to financial resources, scientific expertise and clean technologies necessary to respond to environmental challenges without unnecessary or discriminatory barriers.
He also stressed that independent documentation of environmental damage, scientific assessment of its long-term effects, and arrangements for compensation and rehabilitation should form an integral part of the international response to armed conflicts.
Three priorities for international cooperation
Araghchi proposed three priorities for strengthening international cooperation to prevent environmental destruction and address its consequences.
First, he called for stronger international legal frameworks and clear criteria for identifying, assessing, and responding to cases of extensive and severe environmental damage.
Second, he proposed the establishment of impartial, science-based mechanisms to document environmental damage caused by armed conflicts, assess its long-term consequences, determine applicable legal responsibilities and facilitate compensation.
Third, he urged expanded regional and international cooperation to prevent environmental destruction, restore damaged ecosystems and support countries and communities that lack adequate financial resources or technical capacity.
COP31 offers an opportunity to address the environmental costs of war
Araghchi also identified the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) as an opportunity to draw greater international attention to the environmental and climate consequences of military attacks.
He said Iran was prepared to contribute its scientific, legal and diplomatic capabilities to collective efforts aimed at preventing large-scale environmental destruction, strengthening regional cooperation and promoting international accountability.
The foreign minister emphasized that environmental damage caused by armed conflict cannot be treated as a secondary consequence of war. Its effects on public health, food security, natural resources and the livelihoods of affected communities make it an issue of international concern.
Concluding his remarks, Araghchi called on the international community to ensure that those responsible for environmental destruction do not escape accountability.
“Nature has no voice at the negotiating table or on the battlefield,” he said, stressing that collective action is necessary to prevent environmental devastation from coming at the expense of humanity's future.

articles.title: Iran says US response to conditions for reopening Strait of Hormuz ‘insufficient’
articles.body:
Iran considers Washington’s response to its seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz “insufficient,” a senior Iranian official said, according to the semi-official Tasnim News Agency.
Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said the US had accepted some of Tehran’s conditions, while others remained unclear.
Rezaei said Washington had approached Tehran over the past two months through three channels — Pakistan, Qatar and Iraq — asking Iran to submit its proposals.
About two weeks ago, Iran conveyed seven conditions to the US, explicitly stating that the Strait of Hormuz would not reopen to Washington and no negotiations would take place until those conditions were met, he said.
Rezaei said Tehran was no longer in the process of responding to Washington because the US had already submitted its response, which Iran considered “insufficient.”
“They must clarify the issues that remain ambiguous to us,” he said.
READ: Israeli Democrats leader says killing of Iran’s Ali Khamenei was a ‘mistake’
The report did not detail all seven conditions or specify which ones Washington had accepted.
Rezaei also said the Gulf could not be secure without Iran’s management of the Strait of Hormuz, describing control over the waterway as an “immense source of national wealth and a major national asset.”
He said Iran’s interests extended beyond closing the passage and collecting transit fees.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in late September that Tehran could reopen the strategic waterway within seven days if Washington accepted a proposal conveyed through Qatari mediation.
Under the plan, the US would be expected to take agreed steps during the first four or five days, allowing normal navigation through the strait to resume on the sixth day and negotiations on a final agreement to begin on the seventh.
Tehran’s demands include an end to hostilities, the release of frozen Iranian assets, the lifting of restrictions on Iranian oil exports and an end to the US naval blockade on Iranian ports.
Iran has kept the Strait of Hormuz restricted while demanding that Washington fulfill commitments under a June memorandum of understanding.
Tehran has said the waterway will not fully reopen until its conditions are met and US commitments are implemented.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on Feb. 28. Tehran responded with missile and drone attacks across the region and effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, while Washington later imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports.
Washington and Tehran subsequently signed a memorandum of understanding in June concerning freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, but implementation stalled over disagreements related to security in the strategic waterway.
